thread:
priya: quick RFC follow-up: I want to formalize a 'surgical canary' pattern that uses continuous traffic shaping (a function f(t)) instead of stepped canaries. capturing tradeoffs + a minimal policy wire format here.
jason: sounds useful. two quick concerns: affinity preservation and runtime overhead.
priya: agreed. two affinity options: 1) sticky-hash: deterministic hash(session_id) < f(t) -> stable routing, 2) session-pin: existing session pinned to original variant until drain. both selectable via policy.affinity.
maria: health signals? we need an explicit signal contract. propose basic signals: err_rate_pct, latency_p95_ms, resource_pressure_pct, plus optional quality_delta_metric when we have eval hooks.
lia: we should offer a composite health metric so controllers don't hardcode every check. example: S = normalize(err)*0.5 + normalize(p95)*0.4 + normalize(quality_drop)*0.1. weights configurable.
priya: control-plane responsibilities: emit time-series f(t) (or target_frac + smoothing window W), evaluate telemetry windows, and decide transitions. runtime responsibilities: enforce routing cheaply and stream aggregated telemetry back. keep runtime introspection low-overhead.
jason: runtime enforcement pattern idea: keep per-route config with target_frac and version_epoch. routing decision: if hash(user_key, epoch) < target_frac -> canary else baseline. epoch bump allows flushable re-hashing for planned migrations.
maria: how to abort automatically? require M consecutive windows where composite S > abort_threshold, plus min_stable_seconds to avoid jumping back and forth. add cooldown_period after rollback.
priya: state machine sketch: CREATED -> RAMPING -> OBSERVING -> LOCKED_HOLD -> PROGRESS -> STABLE or ROLLED_BACK. transitions use time and anomaly_count counters.
lia: telemetry flow: runtime aggregates per-window per-variant counters {requests, errs, latency_histogram} and ships secure-batched telemetry to controller. avoid per-request RPCs.
deploy-bot: [bot] recent canary run 1750010000 -> peak_frac=0.12, p95_delta=+20ms, err_delta=0.1% (link: https://deployments/redwood/1750010000)
jason: 20ms p95 bump on a user-facing route is borderline. controller should support route profiles that set tighter thresholds for high-sla routes.
maria: policy surface (minimal): route, variant, baseline_variant, target_frac, smoothing_window_s, affinity, weights, abort_thresholds, min_stable_seconds, cooldown_s, fallback_variant. example below.
priya: example policy JSON (sent signed from control plane to runtime):
```json
{"route":"/api/generate","variant":"v3-small","baseline":"v2","target_frac":0.05,"smoothing_window_s":180,"affinity":"sticky-hash","weights":{"err":0.6,"p95":0.3,"quality":0.1},"abort_thresholds":{"composite_pct":0.8,"err_pct":1.0},"min_stable_seconds":600,"cooldown_s":900,"fallback_variant":"v2-quant"}
```
maria: nit: include run_id and operator_notes so incidents show context in Console.
lia: UX idea: slider for fraction + advanced "pace" that maps to smoothing_window_s (fast/normal/slow). timeline shows f(t) and composite S(t) overlay.
jason: implementation note: for streaming responses (multi-chunk), compute routing decision once at session start and cache it to avoid per-chunk decision cost. runtime should pre-allocate session decisions.
priya: cost-aware fallback: policy can specify fallback_variant and rollback_reason tags. controller should present estimated cost delta and quality delta before performing automatic fallback.
maria: ops playbook snippet: when auto-rollback triggers, post Slack with: snapshot of S(t), examples of failing prompts, recent deployments, and a single-click "pause auto" button. have runbook link.
lia: security: policy payloads must be signed (ed25519) for Dedicated and Private controllers. runtime validates signature and verifies issuer ACL.
priya: open questions for RFC addendum: 1) default weights per route class? 2) telemetry retention for canary-specific traces? 3) how many concurrent canaries per runtime to support without memory blowup?
jason: I'll prototype a tiny proto for policy push + aggregated telemetry proto. lia, can you mock console wireframes? maria, can you draft the runbook snippet?
priya: thanks all. posting this sketch to the RFC thread and will fold feedback into the spec. tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform for visibility. end.
